correctness.rationale: For a J² target, reduction modulo J forces every root into J since the semisimple quotient is a product of fields. Multiplying the paths gives a_i a_{i+1}=u_i and a_i b_{i+1}+b_i a_{i+2}=v_i, with all length-three root coefficients free, even when n=3 and length-three paths return to their starting vertices. On the torus all a_i are units; closing a_i=s_i t^{(-1)^i} requires t²=s_n in odd length and s_n=1 in even length. Dividing b_i by a_i a_{i+1} leaves I+S on a cyclic sequence. Its kernel is controlled by h_{i+1}=-h_i: zero when n and q are odd, one-dimensional otherwise, with image given by the signed-sum condition (unsigned in characteristic two). In even length the normalization produces P/t-tQ=0, including in characteristic two. Counting t, then the normalized length-two solution and then the free length-three vector gives all three fiber laws. The image counts follow by counting admissible u, and in even length by the surjective map v↦(P,Q) with q^{n-2} points over each pair. Summing the fibers gives (q-1)^n q^{2n}; the claimed coincidences at q=2,3 also follow. These are statements about the principal torus, not all of J².
residual_risks: Independent exhaustive path concatenation compared every torus fiber and image size for n=3,4 and q=2,3,4,5; n=5 and q=2,3,4; n=6 and q=2, including genuine F₄ arithmetic. This is finite corroboration only; the path equations establish the universal result. No Lean or expert certification is claimed.

value.rationale: The all-nonzero locus is a natural stratum of the square map, not an arbitrary slice. Counting its lifts reveals a second obstruction invisible after J³ reduction and a qualitative density difference: in odd characteristic the fraction of attainable targets stays one-half for odd cycles but is asymptotic to 1/(2q) for even cycles. The fiber laws additionally separate the even-cycle degeneracy P=Q=0 from square-class compatibility. These are usable exact data for this map, beyond the familiar multiplicative recursion alone.
residual_risks: Does not analyze the boundary of the torus or the square-map image in the whole algebra.
